title: 2011 AMC 12A Problem 21
statement: Let \(f_1(x) = \sqrt{1 - x},\) and for integers \(n \ge 2,\) let \(f_n(x) = f_{n-1}\!\left(\sqrt{n^2 - x}\right).\) If \(N\) is the largest value of \(n\) for which the domain of \(f_n\) is nonempty, the domain of \(f_N\) is \(\{c\}.\) What is \(N + c?\)

solutions.text:
Each step requires \(\sqrt{n^2 - x}\) to lie in the domain of \(f_{n-1}.\) Tracking the domains:

\(f_1: (-\infty, 1].\) \(f_2: \sqrt{4 - x} \in (-\infty, 1] \Rightarrow [3, 4].\) \(f_3: \sqrt{9 - x} \in [3, 4] \Rightarrow [-7, 0].\) \(f_4: \sqrt{16 - x} \in [-7, 0] \Rightarrow \{16\}\) (only the value \(0\) is possible). \(f_5: \sqrt{25 - x} = 16 \Rightarrow \{-231\}.\)

For \(f_6\) we would need \(\sqrt{36 - x} = -231,\) impossible, so the domain is empty. Hence \(N = 5,\) \(c = -231,\) and \(N + c = -226.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Build the domains outward: \(f_n\) needs \(\sqrt{n^2 - x}\) to lie in the domain of \(f_{n-1}\)
The first three domains are \((-\infty,1],\) \([3,4],\) and \([-7,0];\) continue while remembering that a square root is nonnegative
